story.summaryZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿预测周六意大利大奖赛排位赛将是一场"非常接近"的较量，并表示为法拉利在蒙扎夺杆位将是一个"梦想"。

detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿在预测蒙扎排位赛将是一场“非常接近”的较量后，渴望为法拉利夺得意大利大奖赛的“梦想”杆位
乔治·拉塞尔在第二次练习赛中为梅赛德斯拔得头筹，此前查尔斯·勒克莱尔曾在周五第一节练习中领衔法拉利包揽前二，压过刘易斯·汉密尔顿；请观看周六上午11点30分的最后一次练习赛，随后是下午3点的排位赛，天空体育 F1将进行直播
法拉利车手刘易斯·汉密尔顿为一场激烈的意大利大奖赛排位赛做好准备，梅赛德斯的赛车速度持续提升。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿预测，周六的意大利大奖赛排位赛将会是一场“非常接近”的较量，并表示在蒙扎拿下杆位对他来说将是一个“梦想”。
在周五的两节练习赛中，汉密尔顿的成绩都被他的法拉利队友夏尔·勒克莱尔（勒克莱尔）压过，但随着新引擎升级的到来，车队的整体表现表明他们有实力争夺杆位。
在第一节练习赛中，勒克莱尔排在汉密尔顿之前，而梅赛德斯的乔治·拉塞尔在第二节练习赛中速度最快，勒克莱尔位居第二，汉密尔顿仅排第五，落后于基米·安东内利和迈凯伦的兰多·诺里斯。

法拉利将以二对一的优势进入排位赛（下午3点在天空体育 F1直播），因为世界冠军领跑者安东内利已因超出引擎部件配额而受到处罚，无论他在本节比赛中的成绩如何，都将从发车区最后一位起步。
意大利大奖赛周五练习赛的精彩集锦。
汉密尔顿说：“竞争会很激烈，差距非常小。我们要面对迈凯伦和梅赛德斯，它们非常、非常有竞争力。”
“每个周末梅赛德斯的车都真的非常快。这肯定会很艰难，但我们今晚必须埋头努力，看看能不能拿出点什么。”
当被问及在法拉利主场大奖赛上从第一排或杆位发车的可能性时，汉密尔顿回答说：“那是梦想，终极梦想。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿驾驶着一辆罕见的法拉利 F40 抵达意大利大奖赛，并透露这辆车的发动机编号与他的赛车号码相同。
“我们能不能做到是个非常大的问题。今晚我们需要做大量工作，试图弄清楚我们是否在什么地方出了错，以及是否有可以改进的地方——而可以改进的地方有很多。”
“另外，我认为在赛道上出现在正确的时间、正确的位置也会有很大的帮助。”
安东内利预测杆位之争将会非常激烈
尽管他本人并不是杆位争夺的焦点，但安东内利认同汉密尔顿的判断，即这将是一场势均力敌的较量。
这位20岁的意大利车手在积分榜榜首以59分的优势领先拉塞尔和汉密尔顿，而诺里斯以83分之差位居第四。
梅赛德斯车队选择安东内利的主场赛事作为他因超出引擎使用配额而不可避免受罚的最合适场地，因为他们认为，在周日的比赛中从队尾往前追赶，在蒙扎要比今年赛历上剩余的大多数赛道更容易。
梅赛德斯车手基米·安东内利在法拉利于意大利大奖赛练习赛上首次启用一台新引擎后，谈了自己对法拉利的看法。
安东内利说：“今天和平时有点不太一样。更多地专注于长距离测试，所以说实话感觉有点奇怪，但总的来说，今天很不错。”
“我们收集了大量数据，现在期待着接下来几天的表现。
法拉利凭借新引擎确实前进了一步，现在两队的速度不相上下。我们知道他们的赛车在弯道中有多出色，所以明天杆位的争夺肯定会非常激烈。”
“挣扎”中的诺里斯并不指望能争夺杆位
诺里斯满怀信心地来到意大利，此前他在匈牙利和荷兰背靠背夺冠，重新点燃了他卫冕车手总冠军的希望。
然而，这位英国车手情绪低落，因为迈凯伦似乎无法在这条与前两站赛历赛道特性截然不同的赛道上复刻他们近期的状态。
诺里斯说：“不算太好。我在速度上挣扎得厉害多了。”
兰多·诺里斯情绪低落，反思了迈凯伦在周五练习赛中令人沮丧的速度不足。
"在我们本以为会表现好的弯角，我们反而表现很差，而在本以为会表现差的弯角，我们却没有那么差。"
"但我们仍然落后。所以目前处境并不太好。我们会看看今晚能做些什么，但肯定会比之前更艰难。"
"前排很多车手之间的差距非常小。身后的车手也离得不算远，所以他们很容易给我们带来意外。"
"我完全觉得我们没有在争夺杆位的行列中，但我们需要专注于拿到一个体面的成绩。"
detailEn: Lewis Hamilton eyes 'dream' Italian GP pole position for Ferrari after predicting 'very close' Monza qualifying battle

George Russell topped second practice for Mercedes after Charles Leclerc had led Lewis Hamilton in a Ferrari one-two in Friday's first session; watch final practice at 11.30am on Saturday ahead of Qualifying at 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1
Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton braces for a tight Italian GP qualifying as Mercedes continue to find more pace.
Lewis Hamilton is predicting a “very close” battle in Italian Grand Prix qualifying on Saturday for what he says would he says would be a “dream” pole position at Monza.

Hamilton was outperformed by his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in both of Friday's practice sessions but the team's overall performance, following the arrival of a new engine upgrade, suggested they have the pace to compete for pole.

Leclerc topped Hamilton in first practice before Mercedes' George Russell was fastest in the second session, with Leclerc second and Hamilton only fifth behind Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris.

Ferrari are set to go into qualifying, live on Sky Sports F1 at 3pm, with a two-versus-one advantage over Mercedes due to world championship leader Kimi Antonelli having already incurred penalties for exceeding his engine-part allowance that will see him start from the back of the grid regardless of where he finishes the session.
Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Italian Grand Prix.
"It's going to be tight, it's very close," Hamilton said. "We're up against the McLarens and the Mercedes, they are very, very competitive.
"Every weekend the Mercedes is just really, really quick. It'll be tough, for sure, but we need to knuckle down tonight and see if we can pull something out."
Asked about the possibility of starting on the front row or pole position at Ferrari's home race, Hamilton replied: "That's the dream, the ultimate dream.
Lewis Hamilton arrived at the Italian GP in a rare Ferrari F40 and revealed that the car's engine bore the same number as his racing number.

"Whether or not we can is the big, big question. And that's going to take a lot of work tonight to try to figure out if we've gone wrong anywhere and if there's any places we can improve, which there are loads of places we can improve.
"Also, I think being in the right place at the right time on track is going to help a lot."
Antonelli predicts 'tight fight' for pole
Despite not being a factor in the pole contest, Antonelli agrees with Hamilton's assessment that it will be a tight battle.
The 20-year-old Italian leads both Russell and Hamilton by 59 points at the top of the standings, with Norris trailing by 83 points in fourth.

Mercedes have chosen Antonelli's home race as the most suitable venue for him to serve an inevitable penalty for exceeding his engine allowance, due to a belief that fighting back through the field in Sunday's race will be easier at Monza than most other tracks that remain on this year's schedule.
Mercedes Kimi Antonelli gives his thoughts on Ferrari after they debuted a new engine at the Italian GP practice sessions.
Antonelli said: "Today a bit of a different day compared to usual. A lot more focused on long runs so it was a bit weird, not going to lie, but overall, it was a good day.
"We gathered a lot of data and now looking forward to the next few days.

"Ferrari definitely took a step forward with a new engine and now the speeds are the same. We know how good their car is into the corners so, for sure, it's going to be a tight fight for pole tomorrow."
'Struggling' Norris doesn't expect to fight for pole
Norris arrived in Italy full of confidence having claimed back-to-back victories in Hungary and the Netherlands to reignite his hopes of defending his drivers' title.
However, the Brit was downcast after McLaren appeared unable to replicate their recent form at a track with very different characteristics to the previous two on the schedule.
Norris said: "Not very decent. Just struggling a lot more with pace.
A downbeat Lando Norris reflects on McLaren’s frustrating lack of pace in Friday Practice.
"In the corners we expected to be good at we're bad at and in the corners we expected to be bad at, we're not so bad at.
"But we're still off. So not in a great place at the minute. We'll see what we can do overnight but it's going to be tougher than before for sure.
"It's close between a lot of the guys at the top. The guys behind are not that far either so they can easily surprise us.
"I definitely don't feel we are in the fight for pole at all but we need to focus on getting a decent result."
